newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 27.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 27.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

HELSINKI - World advertising growth will slow next year to four to five percent from an estimated six to seven percent this year, Martin Sorrell, CEO of the world's largest advertising and marketing group, WPP Group, is quoted as saying. Expansion will be strongest in Latin America and Asia with double-digit growth rates, Finnish business daily Kauppalehti quotes Sorrell as saying in an interview.

DALLAS - Tobacco companies have agreed to cut cigarette sales to teenagers by 60 percent in the next decade or face huge fines as part of a deal aimed at settling smoking liability issues, The Dallas Morning News reports. The agreement specified that tobacco firms pay $500 million per year for anti-smoking advertising and end all marketing to teen-agers with character advertising such as Joe Camel and Marlboro Man, The Dallas Morning News says.

SEOUL - South Korea's leading carmaker Hyundai Motor Co Ltd says it has borrowed $60 million from Hong Kong-based Banque Indosuez to finance its marketing and advertising efforts in North America and Europe.

HELSINKI - A Finnish dairy association breaks an almost a quarter-century tradition by choosing a boy as its annual "milkgirl" to promote milk. Pekka Yli-Piipari, 22, "a blonde, blue-eyed Viking who charmed the jury with his cheerfulness", was the first man to be chosen in 23 years of campaigning, the Milk and Health Association says.

LONDON - Total advertising expenditure in Britain is expected to grow 6.9 percent in 1997 in constant prices, slightly down from the 7.0 percent growth rate posted in 1996, Zenith Media says. Television revenues, which increased 6.9 percent in 1996 in constant prices, are expected to gain by 5.8 percent this year, says Zenith, the media planning and buying arm of advertising and marketing group Cordiant Plc.

LONDON - Royal Bank of Scotland's Direct Line insurance unit says it has launched a week-long advertising campaign in Britain to publicise its growing mortgage and savings services. The campaignwill run on primetime spots across the ITV commercial television network, Channel Four and BSkyB and be supported by full-page ads in national newspapers.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

SINGAPORE - U.S. software giant Microsoft Corp and Japanese computer maker NEC Corp say they launched an Internet computer service for hotels. Microsoft says the venture, involving an investment of Singapore $30 million ($21 million), over two to three years, would install personal computers in every room in a series of hotels in Singapore and the region. The venture, HotelNet, would use NEC computers running on Microsoft software, NEC says.

PARIS - Time-Warner Inc is set to buy a 35 percent stake in the cable television unit of Generale des Eaux as well as a 10 percent stake in digital satellite television company Canalsatellite, the Les Echos newspaper reports. Citing sources close to the negotiatiions, the paper says Time-Warner Cable would buy the stake in Compagnie Generale de Video Communication, France's second-biggest cable group, from Generale des Eaux.

TOKYO - Internet-based shopping in Japan grew 40-fold in the business year ended on March 31, the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications says. The ministry says Japanese "cybermall" shops on the Internet sold about 28.5 billion yen ($245.1 million) worth of goods during fiscal 1996/97, up from 700 million yen the previous year. But the market was still only one-tenth the size of that of the United States, which grew to 268.68 billion yen during the year, up from 41.7 billion yen.

NEW YORK - International Family Entertainment, owner of the Family Channel that is being courted by News Corp Ltd, has had talks with another possible suitor, Walt Disney Co, the Wall Street Journal reports. The Journal in its electronic edition quotes an unnamed source familiar with the situation as saying Disney recently held acquisition talks with IFE, which is controlled by Pat Robertson and his family.

MIAMI - Knight-Ridder Inc says its operating revenues for April increased 5.8 percent to $271.1 million but would have been flat if 1996 revenues from Knight-Ridder Financial were included. Knight-Ridder Financial was sold in July 1996. Total advertising revenues in April increased 7.9 percent, while they increased 7.2 percent on a year-to-date basis.

NEW YORK - A U.S. district court judge in Texas threw out the bulk of a record $222.7 million libel award against Dow Jones & Co., the company says. U.S. District Court Judge Ewing Werlein threw out $200 million in punitive damages that had been awarded in a libel suit against the company's Wall Street Journal in connection with a story about a now-defunct Houston securities firm, Dow Jones says.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

DUBLIN - Ireland's Waterford Foods says it has agreed improved merger terms from Avonmore Foods Plc to create a dairy giant that would be one of the five biggest milk producers in the world. Avonmore's improved offer values the company at 337 million Irish pounds ($512 million) against an original offer of 281 million, the company says.

HANOI - Australian firm Leda Holdings and a Vietnamese partner have begun a feasibility study into a $200 million tourist resort project near Vietnam's central city of Danang, a project official says. The project involves the construction of three hotels, several villas and apartments and an 18-hole golf course nine km (five miles) south of the city.

WARSAW - American pop star Michael Jackson wants to build a Disneyland-style theme park in Warsaw, Polish state television says. Jackson is hunting for a site bigger than the Warsaw Zoo for a project worth more than $100 million, the Polish news agency PAP quotes the head of the state Foreign Investment Agency, Waldemar Dabrowski, as saying.

JERUSALEM - Israel's anti-trust authorities will soon declare the domestic Coca-Cola bottler a monopoly in carbonated beverages and restrict its sales practices, industry sources say. The sources say authorities would limit Central Bottling Co., which also produces other soft drinks and Carlsberg and Tuborg beers, from signing agreements with stores and restaurants that link sales of its Coca-Cola products to purchases of beer.

BEIJING - China is drafting new pricing policies to encourage the use of unleaded gasoline to reduce vehicle emissions, the Business Weekly says, Price reform, part of a long-term strategy, would ensure that unleaded gasoline cost less than leaded gasoline over the next two years, the newspaper says.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

TOKYO - As Japanese consumers munch on more hamburgers and choose french fries over fried noodles, the world's leading soy sauce maker is looking to the West as the future for oriental flavourings. With limited scope to boost sales in the saturated home market, Kikkoman Corp says it is looking to the United States and Europe for new profit opportunities but is also eyeing China as a potentially promising market closer to home.

LOS ANGELES - Steven Spielberg's dinosaurs trampled movie box office records during the Memorial Day holiday weekend in the U.S. as "The Lost World: Jurassic Park" opened with an estimated $90.1 million for the four-day period, according to studio estimates.

OSAKA - The Ritz-Carlton has arrived in Japan's western capital to lure more Japanese guests -- but industry sources say Osakans, spoiled by a hotel glut, will prove tough customers for the U.S. luxury chain. The Ritz's luxury rooms, furnished with 19th century European antiques, cost 27,000 yen a night, not a shocking amount for Osaka locals who are used to spending money on western fashion brands such as Chanel and Armani.
